text:
Which was earlier: the first Olympic Games or the first modern telephone?
Options: A) telephone B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) Olympic Games

Which is older: the Roman Empire or the printing press in Europe?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) Roman Empire E) printing press

Which came first: the French Revolution or the American Declaration of Independence?
Options: A) both B) neither C) American Declaration D) French Revolution E) cannot determine

Which lasted longer: the Ming dynasty or the Roman Republic?
Options: A) neither B) Ming dynasty C) Roman Republic D) cannot determine E) both

Which was earlier: the end of the Western Roman Empire or the invention of the compass?
Options: A) Western Roman Empire B) compass C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is older: the University of Bologna or the Aztec Empire?
Options: A) Aztec Empire B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) University of Bologna

Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) telephone E) Krakatoa

Which was earlier: the first successful powered flight or the first World War?
Options: A) both B) neither C) powered flight D) World War I E) cannot determine

Which is farther north: London or Berlin?
Options: A) neither B) London C) Berlin D) cannot determine E) both

Which is farther west: Alaska or Hawaii?
Options: A) Alaska B) Hawaii C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which country is larger by area: Argentina or Kazakhstan?
Options: A) Argentina B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) Kazakhstan

Which is older as a written language: Latin or English?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) Latin E) English

Which happened earlier: the first Moon landing or the fall of the Berlin Wall?
Options: A) both B) neither C) Moon landing D) Berlin Wall fall E) cannot determine

Which was founded first: Harvard University or the Royal Society?
Options: A) neither B) Harvard University C) Royal Society D) cannot determine E) both

Which is older: the Great Pyramid or the city of Rome?
Options: A) Great Pyramid B) city of Rome C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which has greater mass: a kilogram of lead or a kilogram of feathers?
Options: A) lead B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) same mass

Which reaches the ground first in a vacuum: a hammer or a feather?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) same time E) hammer

Which is closer to Earth: the Moon or the Sun?
Options: A) both B) neither C) Moon D) Sun E) cannot determine

Which contains more atoms: a mole of water or a mole of iron?
Options: A) neither B) same number C) water D) cannot determine E) both

Which has higher frequency: red light or blue light?
Options: A) blue light B) red light C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which has a longer wavelength: red light or blue light?
Options: A) blue light B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) red light

Which is denser: ice or liquid water?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) liquid water E) ice

Which organ primarily filters waste from blood: the kidneys or the lungs?
Options: A) both B) neither C) kidneys D) lungs E) cannot determine

Which carries oxygen in blood: hemoglobin or insulin?
Options: A) neither B) hemoglobin C) insulin D) cannot determine E) both

Which has more genetic material in a typical human cell: mitochondria or the nucleus?
Options: A) nucleus B) mitochondria C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is warmer in a greenhouse: the inside or the outside?
Options: A) outside B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) inside

Which increases when altitude increases: atmospheric pressure or distance from Earth centre?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) distance from Earth centre E) atmospheric pressure

Which direction does a compass needle point approximately: magnetic north or geographic south?
Options: A) both B) neither C) magnetic north D) geographic south E) cannot determine

Which is a mammal: a dolphin or a shark?
Options: A) neither B) dolphin C) shark D) cannot determine E) both

Which process makes sugar in plants: photosynthesis or respiration?
Options: A) photosynthesis B) respiration C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is larger: 1/3 or 0.3?
Options: A) 0.3 B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) 1/3

Which is larger: 0.9 or 0.09?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) 0.9 E) 0.09

Which is greater: the mean or median of 1, 2, 3, 100?
Options: A) both B) neither C) mean D) median E) cannot determine

Which is more likely with two dice: a total of 7 or a total of 6?
Options: A) neither B) 7 C) 6 D) cannot determine E) both

Which is larger: 2^10 or 10^2?
Options: A) 2^10 B) 10^2 C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is the larger discount: 20% off once or 10% off twice?
Options: A) 10% twice B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) 20% once

Which is faster: doubling a quantity or increasing it by 100%?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) same E) doubling

Which is larger: the perimeter of a square with side 4 or its area?
Options: A) both B) neither C) area D) perimeter E) cannot determine

Which average speed is correct for equal distances at 30 and 60 km/h: 45 or 40 km/h?
Options: A) neither B) 40 C) 45 D) cannot determine E) both

Which is more likely: at least one six in two dice rolls or two sixes?
Options: A) at least one six B) two sixes C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is larger: 10% of 100 or 100% of 10?
Options: A) 100% of 10 B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) same

Which is greater: the chance of heads on one fair coin or two heads in two tosses?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) one head E) two heads

Which is closer to zero: -0.2 or 0.1?
Options: A) both B) neither C) 0.1 D) -0.2 E) cannot determine

Which is larger: a 50% increase followed by a 50% decrease, or the original?
Options: A) neither B) original C) the changed value D) cannot determine E) both

Which is the median of 1, 2, 100: 2 or 34.33?
Options: A) 2 B) 34.33 C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is more informative about a skewed dataset: the mean or the median?
Options: A) mean B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) median

Which protects a password database better: salted hashing or plain encryption with one shared key?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) salted hashing E) shared-key encryption

Which does HTTPS primarily protect: transport confidentiality or endpoint malware?
Options: A) both B) neither C) transport confidentiality D) endpoint malware E) cannot determine

Which is safer for an untrusted file: parsing it as data or executing it as code?
Options: A) neither B) parsing as data C) executing as code D) cannot determine E) both

Which is usually stronger: a long unique password or a short reused password?
Options: A) long unique password B) short reused password C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which does a checksum provide: integrity evidence or proof of author identity?
Options: A) author identity B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) integrity evidence

Which stops a stolen session cookie more directly: cookie invalidation or a new login password?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) cookie invalidation E) new password

Which is safer against SQL injection: parameterized queries or string concatenation?
Options: A) both B) neither C) parameterized queries D) string concatenation E) cannot determine

Which is more private on a network: encrypted DNS or plain DNS?
Options: A) neither B) encrypted DNS C) plain DNS D) cannot determine E) both

Which prevents all phishing: two-factor authentication or neither?
Options: A) neither B) two-factor authentication C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

Which is more resistant to guessing: a random 16-character password or a memorable 8-character password?
Options: A) memorable 8-character password B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) random 16-character password

If all A are B and no B are C, can any A be C?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) no E) yes

If some A are B and some B are C, must some A be C?
Options: A) both B) neither C) no D) yes E) cannot determine

If a test is positive 99% of the time for sick people, does that alone give the chance of sickness after a positive?
Options: A) neither B) no C) yes D) cannot determine E) both

If two events are mutually exclusive and both non-zero, can they be independent?
Options: A) no B) yes C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

If a treatment works in every subgroup, must it work better overall?
Options: A) yes B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) no

If a correlation is strong, does it by itself prove causation?
Options: A) cannot determine B) both C) neither D) no E) yes

If an argument has a true conclusion, must its reasoning be valid?
Options: A) both B) neither C) no D) yes E) cannot determine

If a coin landed heads five times, is tails guaranteed next?
Options: A) neither B) no C) yes D) cannot determine E) both

If a model is accurate on average, must it be accurate for every subgroup?
Options: A) no B) yes C) cannot determine D) both E) neither

If two claims are both plausible, does that make both true?
Options: A) yes B) cannot determine C) both D) neither E) no
